title: Capture golden state
summary: Capture a new golden through the governed operation to seal current cause-bearing probes. On macOS it first asks a running Safari to quit and waits for it, never force-quitting, so Safari's state is on disk; Linux and WSL capture does the same for the desktop Chromium, refusing test_machine_sign_in_app_quit_not_proved when it stays open; macOS harness logins, browser identities and Safari's cookie store stay outside the archive. Saving a completed harness sign-in is this same capture. Required Linux teaching also excludes desktop Chromium sign-ins from every golden and preserves the existing ~/snap/chromium/common/chromium store only when present after Chromium quits; an older golden must never restore stale browser sign-in state. This snap-store exclusion is operator-required candidate teaching; source implementation, real reset/sign-in proof and release evidence remain pending. Observed status describes the existing capture behavior, not proof of the new exclusion. Capture refuses golden_capture_insufficient_space before writing when the destination filesystem cannot hold the home, and after the new golden is registered it deletes every retired snapshot except that golden and its probes and manifest. An undeclared nonzero probe exit retries once with both attempts retained; a declared failure stops immediately.
